hot.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
hot.summary: ScaleVLA connects a frozen 552-billion-parameter vision-language backbone to a trainable action head, which converts image, instruction, and robot-state features into action chunks without generating text. In fixed-budget benchmarks, it reaches 87.8% LIBERO-Goal success with 10 demonstrations per task, versus 85.6% for a 2B policy with 50. Its comparisons do not isolate parameter count from model-family differences.

hot.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
hot.summary: Stream of Belief treats multi-agent reasoning as repeated exchange and revision of continuous internal beliefs. Agents alternate global interaction, using other agents’ beliefs, with local refinement based on their own belief and the problem; belief tokens mix embeddings from the top 50 candidate tokens. On GPQA-Diamond, SoB scores 44.9% versus LatentMAS’s 34.3%, below debate’s 53.0%.

hot.title: $π^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
hot.summary: π⁴ reconstructs moving scenes from uncalibrated images or video, estimating geometry, camera poses, scale, and motion. It predicts image-space correspondences and lifts them onto reconstructed target-view geometry to place tracks in 3D. The paper reports the best overall average geometry rank (3.00) and competitive tracking results, but this rank does not establish superior metric-scale accuracy.

hot.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
hot.summary: K2-Horizon releases six models with checkpoints, logs, training data, and code. The authors train four dense and sparse models on a shared 22-trillion-token corpus; their normalized loss curves nearly overlap, though normalization aligns endpoints. At final mid-training, 36B-A4B scores 86.9 on 0-shot MMLU versus 88.1 for dense 32B, with about one-seventh as many active backbone parameters per token.

hot.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
hot.summary: The paper examines whether noisy evaluations limit frozen-weight agent evolution. It measures both candidate quality and selectors’ ability to identify better artifacts, using skill pools and benchmark comparisons. On Terminal-Bench, a 100-skill pool exceeds an equal-quality null by 3.4 pp, while one-rollout selection is statistically indistinguishable from chance. The evidence concerns tested frozen-weight settings, not all self-improvement.

hot.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
hot.summary: The authors introduce the Lattice, adding persistent per-layer states that recur across tokens alongside the Transformer’s vertical residual stream. These states condition attention and the MLP without adding token positions or KV-cache entries. After 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens, its 405.6M-parameter model reaches perplexity 14.40 versus 15.41 for a 406.7M baseline at approximately matched forward compute: 0.72 versus 0.71 GFLOP/token.

hot.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
hot.summary: Sage S2.1 Flash combines scientific inputs, text and images in one model context, and trains actions and answers against checks of execution results, environment changes or submitted artifacts. Its evaluations span 33 benchmarks. On MLE-bench Lite, it scores 90.3 HumanRank, ahead of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at 89.2. These results support benchmark capability, but not reliable end-to-end scientific workflows.

hot.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
hot.summary: ALOHA Lightning speeds robot manipulation by collecting demonstrations through direct, hands-on guidance of the robot arms and adapting learned policies for autonomous execution. It blends overlapping action chunks to smooth motion and masks operator regions in training and deployment images. On battery insertion, it achieves 85% whole-task success in 5.70 seconds; toss-and-catch takes 1.85 seconds with 50% success.

hot.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
hot.summary: The authors study how Qwen3-VL-8B plans visual list answers. They find that it binds written answers to image locations and uses the last answer’s position as a spatial cursor to select what to inspect next. In a controlled synthetic task, this cursor predicts the matching letter after panel 4 in 98.4% of cases at layer 20, not general list accuracy.

hot.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy$\unicode{8211}$Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
hot.summary: Kumo Tabular predicts labels from labeled rows using a pretrained encoder and transformer, without task-specific weight updates or hyperparameter search. Its encoder alternates column and row attention before compressing rows for in-context prediction. Kumo Tabular-L ranks first on primary metrics across eight benchmarks, but Elo intervals overlap top non-Kumo results, and performance is weaker on grouped splits and tables above 100K training rows.

hot.title: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
hot.summary: VSpark accelerates autoregressive vision-language-action decoding by reusing target predictions from rejected draft branches as candidates under corrected prefixes. It trains the draft with perturbed robot states and target-feature alignment, while keeping exact target verification unchanged. On π₀-FAST across LIBERO, VSpark reaches mean committed length 3.94 versus DSpark’s 3.16 and decoding speedup 1.93× versus 1.60×; these are simulated decoding-time results, not demonstrated task-success or real-world control-frequency gains.

hot.title: stable-envs-v1: Fast and Reproducible Environments with Controllable Variations
hot.summary: The authors introduce stable-envs, a library that advances simulator states and renders images on the training GPU rather than moving stored frames from CPU memory. It supports controlled appearance changes from saved states, with explicit visual factors in 78 of 80 classes. Across four tested environments, LeWM training is faster; on PushT, throughput rises from 4.58 to 6.09 steps per second, while planning success averages 94.0% versus 93.3% over three seeds.

hot.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
hot.summary: MovieRoll generates continuous videos across prompted events by jointly denoising neighboring chunks and selectively retaining historical attention states. It trains a multi-step base with windowed training, then distills it into a five-step generator. On the 60-second, six-event HeliosBench task, MovieRoll-Distilled scores 6.492 versus 5.880 for Helios-Base; MovieRoll-Base was not evaluated at this duration, and generation remains below real-time playback.

hot.title: Robotic Reward Models in the Foundation-Model Era
hot.summary: The authors survey 114 robotic reward methods into five families based on what their outputs judge. They test evaluators on an offline benchmark that separates task state from motion and camera evidence. GPT-6.1 Sol’s final scores select the most-complete execution in 85% of 28 tasks, but dense scores often miss task-state changes; this does not demonstrate improved robot policies.

hot.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
hot.summary: Invoker-Render turns structural video proxies, appearance references, and language into controllable-looking video for offline creation and causal streaming, using a shared interface for whole-clip and four-step causal rendering. Its ProForcing training moves from data-anchored histories to self-generated rollouts. In 140 streaming comparisons, it beats four-step SolarRenderer in 88, ties 2, and loses 50; this does not isolate the cause or demonstrate infinite generation.

hot.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: The method combines image STEM, image perception, and video reasoning by training domain experts, distilling their feedback into one student’s own responses, then applying reward-based reinforcement learning. On 21 benchmarks, the student scores 75.2 accuracy across eight sampled responses, versus 74.4 for mixed-domain training from the base model; a further stage reaches 75.9, though not every domain or benchmark improves.

hot.title: Pixel is All You Need
hot.summary: The authors train a pixel-only model to reason by updating a canvas frame by frame. On Compute Then Paint, it reaches 98.1% test accuracy at 130M parameters, compared with 31.1% for direct answering trained for four times as many steps. Success requires correct arithmetic, region labels and marks, and painting with IoU of at least 0.8; results cover generated tasks.

hot.title: SWE-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Coding
hot.summary: SWE-OPD trains a coding agent using teacher scores on its own repository actions and observations, while masking tool outputs from the loss. Online Qwen3.5-9B with Qwen3.6-27B supervision reaches 39.4% on SWE-bench Pro versus a 35.9% baseline. Yet GLM-4.5-Air trained with RKL shows rising repetition despite falling loss, unlike ST in that run, motivating behavior checks beyond loss.

hot.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
hot.summary: The authors test surface-code stability on a 105-qubit processor, scaling patches from 3×3 to 7×7 to reveal persistent faults across correction cycles. Measurements and modeling implicate data-qubit heating into |3⟩; a walking circuit suppresses its long-cycle effects. At 60 cycles, its logical-error upper bound is ≤3.20×10⁻⁸, but it performs worse at low cycle counts and remains limited by radiation bursts.

hot.title: DuoFlow: Towards Synchronized Speech and Motion Generation with Fine-Grained Control
hot.summary: DuoFlow jointly generates speech and full-body motion from a transcript, voice description, and coarse or temporally ordered body-part motion instruction. It uses paired MotionSpeech examples and bidirectional information exchange between audio and motion streams. On MotionSpeech, it reports 4.71% word error rate and 87.43%/90.40% instruction PairAcc, while Match-TTSG has lower BC Gap, 0.06 versus 0.14.

likes.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
likes.summary: The authors compare multimodal model designs by separating visual pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and where image processing occurs, while controlling data and compute. At the longest budget for a 1.7B backbone, in-fusion reaches 49.2% Avg. VQA, versus 48.9% for a scratch encoder and 44.8% without dedicated vision processing. These dense-backbone experiments do not rule out benefits from external data.

likes.title: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier: Scaling Law for Latent Feedback Transformers on Repeated Data
likes.summary: The authors test latent feedback, which passes each token’s top-layer state into the next token’s input, against a repeated-data Transformer. At matched validation loss, it uses 48% less compute (60M, 400 UTPP, two epochs) and 41% less unique data (271M, 100 UTPP, three epochs). It can lose when data is scarce; evidence covers one recipe, dataset and model ladder.

likes.title: Interpretable Weight-Space Programming Builds Transparent Transformers and Brain Encoding Models
likes.summary: iWSP lets a coding agent write interpretable model features directly and revise them using a fixed evaluator’s score, rather than learning feature weights through backpropagation. In brain encoding, the evaluator fits ridge-regression readouts. The visual model outperforms interpretable baselines on held-out data in early and ventral cortex, but trails AlexNet in ventral cortex; story-position features also reveal scan-edge timing.

likes.title: Weight-Space Reading
likes.summary: The authors test whether a reader can predict behavioral effects of model-weight edits without running the target, comparing access to weights and Python tools with text descriptions of the same edits. On subtle edits, the 27-billion-parameter reader scores 0.730 balanced accuracy with weights versus 0.578 with text alone. This result rests on 10 changed edits and 18 changed behavior labels.

likes.title: SLAM Dunk: A Recipe for Long-Horizon Egocentric SLAM in the Wild
likes.summary: SLAM Dunk improves offline visual–inertial bundle adjustment by allowing stereo-camera calibration to vary over time and fitting gyroscope scale and axis-misalignment errors. On the held-out LaMAria leaderboard, it exceeded Aria in three of five categories, including Medium (78.9 versus 78.5 CP), but its equally weighted category mean was lower (75.46 versus 75.86). This supports near-parity on the benchmark, not an overall win.

likes.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
likes.summary: The authors train a robot-use model with reinforcement learning on simulated tasks, using task-success rewards and a shared end-effector pose interface. The model observes camera images and robot state, then proposes each move. It reaches 74.4% on LIBERO and succeeds in 18 of 30 real YAM trials, versus none for its base model; evidence is limited to tested tasks.

likes.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn’t Need Transformers
likes.summary: The paper studies WSP, where an LLM writes another model’s weights directly, without gradient training. The authors let LLMs choose model structures; three writers independently produce sparse fact tables. Claude Opus 5.5’s first-generation table reaches 50.8% ARC accuracy with 0.94 million parameters, about 1,800 times fewer than the 1.72-billion-parameter Qwen3-1.7B model written by that writer. The finding is limited to untrained models and multiple-choice recall.

likes.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
likes.summary: Ropedia Xperience 2 combines real scene scans with head-mounted human task recordings, registering video and estimated motion to the scan. The captures support simulated scenes and robot policy rollouts. In one converted home simulation, a robot completed an eight-step mug-to-microwave-to-bedroom task from all 30 held-out start states. This demonstrates simulated success for one task, not real-world performance or a scaling law.

likes.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
likes.summary: The authors present Gamer, a vision-language-action system that reads game screens and issues keyboard-and-mouse actions while pursuing long tasks. It combines task instructions, persistent summaries, online reinforcement learning, and real-time inference. On held-out Honkai: Star Rail tasks within a familiar game, Gamer-RL reaches 83.6% milestone-level accuracy versus 69.1% for Gamer-SFT; this is not full-quest completion or unseen-game transfer.

likes.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
likes.summary: PixVid adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to generate pixels one frame at a time, replacing temporally compressed VAE latents with pixel patches. It predicts clean video and aligns controls to individual frames, avoiding block waits. On text-to-video generation, it scores 84.78 VBench versus 84.05 for Wan2.1, while control latency falls from 495 ms to 34 ms at lower throughput.

likes.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
likes.summary: CRAM (Compact Reasoning Associative Memory) learns a pairwise energy over candidate puzzle boards and searches for low-energy solutions rather than repeatedly predicting digits. It guides cell-by-cell search while keeping clues fixed. It solves 99.996% of 412,786 Sudoku-Extreme test puzzles, with 282-fold fewer inference FLOPs than EBR at matched accuracy; these structured-puzzle results do not establish general reasoning ability.

likes.title: Beyond the Training Distribution: A Survey of Reasoning Generalization in Large Language Models
likes.summary: The authors survey how large language models generalize reasoning procedures across explicit distribution shifts. They organize methods by whether they act during training, inference, or architecture, and review behavioral, mechanistic, and theoretical evidence. The survey finds that methods can help in particular settings, but none consistently generalizes across shifts; differences among studies preclude controlled comparisons.

likes.title: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
likes.summary: The authors introduce dataset distillation that optimizes class distributions in frozen feature spaces rather than classifier losses. Synthetic images are pulled toward real examples and separated from one another across augmented views. With ten noise-initialized images per ImageNet-1k class, a ResNet-18 reaches 27.0 ± 0.2% top-1 accuracy, versus 11.7 ± 0.3% for the strongest noise-initialized baseline; the results do not establish lower overall compute.

likes.title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
likes.summary: LoopFill accelerates looped-model decoding by combining retrieved continuations and shallow-loop predictions in one draft tree. These guesses start later token computations early, while full-depth verification selects tokens and preserves the autoregressive output distribution. Under greedy decoding, decode-latency speedup averages 5.85× across seven benchmarks for Ouro-2.6B, versus 4.19× for LoopAhead; it does not measure end-to-end throughput.

likes.title: Knowledge Distillation for Language Models: A Survey of Training Contexts and Supervision
likes.summary: The survey organizes language-model distillation by training-context provenance and version lag, distinguishing external, current-policy, lagged-policy, and mixed-policy supervision. It separates context origin from supervision and update choices, and uses LM-KD to compare seven scenarios. In one reported Qwen3-8B example, Lightning OPD cuts GPU-hours from 120 to 30, but this does not establish a general advantage for reused contexts.

likes.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
likes.summary: Singularity-Bench tests agents’ ability to build systems across six phases of AI development. Agents receive minimal code and fixed work budgets; their systems are compared with mature references on the same hardware. Among 11 agents, Opus 5.5 with Claude Code is the only one reported to match or beat references on all six tasks, with a Singularity-Index of 1.251. The benchmark is a proxy for recursive self-improvement, not a full test.

likes.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
likes.summary: ScaleVLA connects a frozen 552-billion-parameter vision-language backbone to a trainable action head, which converts image, instruction, and robot-state features into action chunks without generating text. In fixed-budget benchmarks, it reaches 87.8% LIBERO-Goal success with 10 demonstrations per task, versus 85.6% for a 2B policy with 50. Its comparisons do not isolate parameter count from model-family differences.

likes.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: JEV uses one fixed decision model as Actor, Judge, and Teacher: it scores rollout actions after the trajectory, and centered scores augment GRPO outcome advantages during training. For Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Hindsight + Progress raises ALFWorld All success from 72.8% ± 3.6 to 82.9% ± 2.9, and WebShop success from 56.8% ± 3.8 to 71.4% ± 0.7, in two text environments with episodes capped at 30 and 15 actions, respectively.

likes.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
likes.summary: SALA uses language descriptions to align unpaired human and robot video clips, with robot action reconstruction anchoring robot representations. Human video supports both general pre-training and task-specific post-training. Up to 2,678 equivalent pre-training hours reduced held-out action-prediction error by 2.21% versus SALA without human video; task-specific human demonstrations increased average robot success from 53.75% to 72.5%, with tokenizer annotation required.

likes.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
likes.summary: The authors present Embodied System 2, a framework in which a foundation model and embodied harness interpret intent, call robot capabilities, and verify physical outcomes. In RT-Safe, eight VLMs had 91.3% completion in paused simulation versus 94.1% in real time, but safe success fell from 19.8% to 0.7%; timing alone was not isolated.
